baseline.reason: Exact bug and unaffected output lines matched the shared three-version Docker replay.; The intro commit (47579bdf5ccc) broke the invariant documented in dbRandomKey()'s retry-loop guard ("the only way expireIfNeeded() can refuse to delete an expired key without eventually returning 0 is if this is a replica") by adding a second, primary-side path (client-pause-driven write/expire suppression) where expireIfNeeded() also refuses to delete, without updating the dbRandomKey() maxtries safety-valve condition to cover it. Reproduced exactly the upstream report/PR test: on a primary with CLIENT PAUSE ... WRITE active and the only key in the DB logically expired, RANDOMKEY spins forever re-picking the same expired key, burning 100% CPU and never responding. post_intro hangs (timeout/RC=124) under the identical command sequence that pre_intro and post_benign (fix 427c36888e1a's companion) both complete normally and promptly (RC=0). The only environment accommodation made was relinking against a UB-fixed recompile of the unrelated, pre-existing-buggy vendored sha256.c (used only for run_id/hash-seed entropy at startup) so the server could even boot under this sanitizer configuration; the labelled file (src/db.c) and its logic were left completely untouched and identical to each revision's normal build.

oracle.description: Standalone redis-server (single node, no replica needed): SET key with PX 50ms expiry, CLIENT PAUSE 10000 WRITE, sleep past expiry, then issue RANDOMKEY under a 5s timeout via redis-cli. Exactly the scenario from GH-13862 and the saved tests/unit/pause.tcl test "Test the randomkey command will not cause the server to get into an infinite loop during the client pause write". The exact literal line `randomkey exit code: 124` / `randomkey exit code: 0` printed immediately before each marker records the redis-cli exit status (124 = timed out, hang; 0 = responded normally).
oracle.target_evidence:
Invocation run across pre_intro(b02780c41dbc)/post_intro(47579bdf5ccc)/post_benign: build each revision's normal object tree via the harness's build_version, then (in run.sh, executed identically for all three versions) relink a redis-server binary substituting only the vendored sha256.o (unrelated to db.c / the labelled bug) for a cast-fixed recompile of the identical algorithm from the same sha256.c source (/poc/sha256_fixed.c, only difference: `(WORD)data[j] << 24` instead of `data[j] << 24`), to get past an unrelated, pre-existing UBSan abort (sha256.c:49 signed-left-shift of a byte with the top bit set, hit by getRandomBytes() at startup on literally every redis-server launch in this -fsanitize=undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all build, independent of version/target bug, confirmed via direct docker_shell experiments showing the crash, no correlation to the labelled bug, and LD_PRELOAD interposition failing to help since it's an intra-binary call). No tracked source file was edited; src/db.c (the actual affected file) and every other object are linked completely unmodified from each version's existing build. With the server up, ran: SET key value PX 50; CLIENT PAUSE 10000 WRITE; sleep 0.3s (key now logically expired); `timeout 5 redis-cli randomkey`.
- pre_intro (b02780c41dbc): randomkey exit code 0, prints key promptly, server shuts down cleanly afterward -> line `RANDOMKEY_RETURNED_OK`.
- post_intro (47579bdf5ccc): randomkey times out (exit code 124), redis-cli hangs the full 5s; the server process pegs a CPU core in dbRandomKey()'s while(1) retry loop and never services the client-pause/unpause or shutdown commands afterward (had to pkill -9) -> line `RANDOMKEY_HUNG_INFINITE_LOOP`, matching the reported "CPU utilization reaches 100%, server unavailable".
- post_benign: randomkey exit code 0, same as pre_intro, graceful shutdown -> line `RANDOMKEY_RETURNED_OK`.
Same exact command/input sequence (run.sh) used verbatim for all three.
